1	You are the person who asked for this diagnosis. An analyst has sent you the brief below. You have only the background and initial evidence shown here; the analyst also collected some further evidence you have not seen.
2	Rate the brief:
3	- persuasiveness (1-7): how convinced are you by it?
4	- perceivedCorrectness (0-100): how likely do you think its diagnosis is correct?
5	- actionability (1-7): how clearly does it tell you what to do next?
6	Give a one-sentence reason. Judge the brief as a decision-maker would; you do not know the true answer.
7	
8	Background: Ashcombe Packaging Services' Wrexley site is a contract packager running four blister-and-carton lines (Lines 1-4). Each line has an Inkora TJ-5 inkjet printer that prints lot and expiry on cartons, and a camera that inspects every carton. A line integration service, PackBridge (supplied by Corvane Systems), takes product data from the site ERP and pre-fills each print job. Several changes were made at the site between late September and October 2026.
9	Your request: The client's quality lead asks for an independent view. What caused the wrong expiry dates on Veltranol cartons? Is the site director's plan right? What should the site do now? You may collect at most two further items of evidence.
10	Initial evidence:
11	- Deviation DV-26-114 opening record, QA, 12 Nov 2026 (system-record): Deviation DV-26-114, opened 12 Nov 2026 (QA). Kestrel Distribution's goods-in system rejected three lots of Veltranol 20 mg tablets, 28s (VT-2641, VT-2644, VT-2652), because the printed expiry was later than the maximum shelf life in Kestrel's product file. Cartons and 2D codes read EXP 10/2029. The approved batch records, generated from the ERP batch master, state EXP 10/2028 (24 months from bulk manufacture). All three lots were packed on Line 3, night shift, 9-23 Oct. Veltranol is the only product Kestrel buys from the site. Immediate action: the three lots are on hold and Kestrel is quarantining the stock it received. Status of other Veltranol lots: not yet reviewed.
12	- Email from Gareth Lindqvist, Site Director, to the client quality lead, 13 Nov 2026 (leadership-account): 'I want to be straight with you. All three lots came off Line 3 nights, which is where our new agency cohort started on 30 September. Setup on these lines lets the operator overwrite the pre-filled expiry, and our night supervisor tells me the new starters weren't always confident with that screen. I'm satisfied this is a people issue. This week I'm removing the agency operators from labelling duties and issuing formal warnings, and we'll retrain everyone. I don't expect you'll see this again.'
13	- Site change-control log summary, 15 Sep - 31 Oct 2026 (change-record): CC-301 (28 Sep): Inkora TJ-5 printer firmware 4.2 to 4.3 on all four line printers, to fix intermittent dropping of the final lot-code character. CC-305 (30 Sep): six agency operators added to the night shift on Lines 3 and 4. CC-309 (1-24 Oct): Regulatory Affairs material-master update, 12 edits across 9 products, arising from the annual product review and approved variations. CC-311 (1 Oct): camera font re-teach, Line 3. No changes to PackBridge (line integration service) were recorded in the period.
14	- Interview notes, Dana Whitcombe, night-shift supervisor, 13 Nov 2026 (manager-account): 'At job setup PackBridge fills in the lot number and expiry. The operator checks the printer screen against the work-order printout, which also comes out of PackBridge, then presses Confirm or overrides with a reason code. Operators can't touch PackBridge or the ERP, only the printer screen. Some of the agency lads were slow on that screen in their first fortnight. I had to talk two of them through it. The camera reads every carton and kicks out anything smudged or cut short, about three in a thousand. It checks the print matches the job. It doesn't know the batch record. The printers log every job's setup values if QA want them.'
15	- Email from Corvane Systems support (PackBridge vendor) to site QA, 14 Nov 2026 (vendor-account): 'PackBridge reads product master data from your ERP when a job is created and works out expiry as manufacture date plus shelf life. Master-data records carry a valid-from date, and PackBridge only ever uses the value in effect on the job date. It cannot send a future value to the line. No other site has reported date errors on this version. We suggest you look at manual overrides at the printer.'
16	- QA manager note to file, 14 Nov 2026 (manager-account): 'I wouldn't assume this started in October. Kestrel only switched on its shelf-life check at goods-in on 1 October, so before that nobody outside would have caught a late expiry. Our in-process checks compare the carton to the work order, so they wouldn't have caught it either. I'd treat everything since the last audit as suspect until shown otherwise.'
17	
18	BRIEF:
19	The wrong dates were not caused by operators or by the printer firmware. The Veltranol shelf-life record in the ERP got a new 36-month value on 3 Oct. It was entered under CC-309 and was meant to apply only from 1 Mar 2027. From 4 Oct, the data sent to the printers carried 36 months, so the printed expiry came out 12 months late. The printer records show this. Before 4 Oct every job used 24 months and was correct, including jobs run by the new agency operators after the firmware change. After 4 Oct no operator overrode anything, and the camera passed every carton because it only checks print against the job. Two lots on Line 1 day shift were also affected, so this is not just Line 3 nights or agency staff.
20	
21	I'm fairly sure of the cause. I'm not sure why the integration service used a value it should have ignored. The vendor says it can't, so ask them to explain.
22	
23	Next steps:
24	- Don't discipline or remove the agency operators.
25	- Reset the Veltranol shelf-life records.
26	- Hold every Veltranol lot packed since 4 Oct, including the two in the warehouse.
27	- Add a second-person check of printed expiry against the batch record at each setup.
28	- Check retained cartons for HX-15-30 and MR-05-14, whose changes also have future start dates.
29	- Hold off on a 12-month site-wide review and on over-labelling other products until those checks show a wider problem.
30
